name: Structuring ADU Design Payments Safely in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How can I structure payments to an ADU design contractor in Los Angeles County to protect myself if the project is delayed or canceled?
mainEntity.text: How can I structure payments to an ADU design contractor in Los Angeles County to protect myself if the project is delayed or canceled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payment structure is one of the few levers homeowners control when hiring an ADU design contractor in Los Angeles County. Aim to align payments with deliverables instead of paying large sums upfront. A common structure might be a modest retainer at signing, a payment at completion of feasibility and as-builts, another at concept design approval, a larger one at completion of construction documents including structural and Title 24, and a final payment at permit submittal or approval. Avoid contracts that demand most of the fee before you see detailed drawings or before the city accepts your application. Make sure the agreement includes clear termination clauses: what you owe if you stop the project, what you receive (CAD files, PDFs, reports), and whether you can use those documents with another designer or builder. Ask for language addressing prolonged delays, such as city moratoriums or personal finance changes, so you can pause without automatically owing the full fee. Also clarify whether hourly services beyond a defined scope require written approval before billing. This milestone-based approach lets you evaluate quality at each step and reduces your risk if the project becomes infeasible or you decide not to proceed.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tie ADU design payments to milestones like feasibility completion, concept approval, construction documents, and permit submittal. Limit upfront retainers, avoid paying 100% before permit approval, and include clear termination terms, work-product ownership, and refund or stop-work provisions for major delays or scope changes.
